extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of art and architecture; art historians, critics, and architects interested in Byzantine religious art and Venetian buildings
extracted.subtask_short: analyzing Byzantine religious art and architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Reading- and practice-oriented criteria for evaluating the religious efficacy, iconography, materiality, and proportional harmony of Byzantine mosaics, frescoes, and palaces (with emphasis on St. Mark's and contemporary Venetian examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective religious art lies between idol-fashioning and magnificent craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective religious art, therefore, has always lain, and I believe must always lie, between the two extremes--of barbarous idol-fashioning on one side, and magnificent craftsmanship on the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious art should avoid the crude literalism of idol-making and also avoid becoming mere display of technical virtuosity that distracts from sacred subject; it should retain a devotional, didactic character while being well-executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate media for religious art
rubrics_metrics.description: It consists partly in missal painting, and such book-illustrations ... partly in glass-painting; partly in rude sculpture ... partly in mosaics; and partly in the frescoes and tempera pictures ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different branches (missal painting, glass, sculpture, mosaics, fresco/tempera) serve different devotional functions; choose the medium that best suits scale, visibility, and liturgical purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale luminous mosaics command worshipper's attention
rubrics_metrics.description: The great mosaics of the twelfth and thirteenth centuries covered the walls and roofs of the churches with inevitable lustre; they could not be ignored or escaped from; their size rendered them majestic, their distance mysterious, their color attractive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For strong religious impact, artworks should be large, luminous, and placed so they cannot be bypassed; scale, distance, and color contribute to majesty and mystery and thus to devotional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid displaying evidences of technical skill that distract from subject
rubrics_metrics.description: They were not adorned with any evidences of skill or science, such as might withdraw the attention from their subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique should serve the subject; visible ostentation of craft or scientific showmanship that pulls attention away from the theological message is an artistic fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inscriptions abundantly and legibly as didactic scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: Our eyes are now familiar and wearied with writing; and if an inscription is put upon a building, unless it be large and clear, it is ten to one whether we ever trouble ourselves to decipher it. But the old architect was sure of readers. He knew that every one would be glad to decipher all that he wrote; ... the more he gave them, the more grateful would the people be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inscriptions should be numerous, clear, and legible; architects/artists should expect viewers to read and receive theological instruction from texts carved or painted on the building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural program should instruct viewers in stages (catechetical sequencing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A large atrium or portico is attached to two sides of the church, a space which was especially reserved for unbaptized persons and new converts. It was thought right that, before their baptism, these persons should be led to contemplate the great facts of the Old Testament history ... the order of the subjects in this series being very nearly the same as in many Northern churches, but significantly closing with the Fall of the Manna ... to mark to the catechumen the insufficiency of the Mosaic covenant for salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange imagery in chronological/theological order appropriate to the viewer's spiritual status (e.g., pre-baptismal instruction in the atrium, post-baptismal revelations within), so that the building itself teaches doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate text and image at entry points to reinforce saving doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: Over its main entrance he saw, on looking back, a mosaic of Christ enthroned, ... Christ is represented as holding a book open upon his knee, on which is written: 'I AM THE DOOR; BY ME IF ANY MAN ENTER IN, HE SHALL BE SAVED.' On the red marble fillet ... is written ... 'WHO HE WAS, AND FROM WHOM HE CAME, AND AT WHAT PRICE HE REDEEMED THEE, AND WHY HE MADE THEE ... DO THOU CONSIDER.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place decisive scriptural statements and complementary imagery at entrances and thresholds so that everyday acts of entry function as continual reminders of salvation and doctrinal truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dome and cupola iconography should express central theological truths
rubrics_metrics.description: The mosaic of the first dome ... represents the effusion of the Holy Spirit ... From the central symbol of the Holy Spirit twelve streams of fire descend upon the heads of the twelve apostles ... the words of [the hymn] are continued around the border of the dome, uniting praise to God for the gift of the Spirit, with welcome to the redeemed soul received into His Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose central symbols and surrounding inscriptions in cupolas/domes to teach and emphasize core doctrines (e.g., Trinity, sanctification, mission) appropriate to that architectural locus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial hierarchy of scenes should mirror theological priority
rubrics_metrics.description: After thus hearing praise ... it was thought fittest that the worshipper should be led to contemplate ... three facts ... namely that Christ died, that He rose again, and that He ascended into heaven ... The second cupola itself ... is entirely occupied by the subject of the Ascension. ... The third cupola, that over the altar, represents the witness of the Old Testament to Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the building's vertical and axial ordering (cupolas, vaults, chapels) to place theologically primary events in the most prominent spatial positions so that liturgical and visual emphasis align.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary imagery should symbolically reinforce central messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneath the circle of the apostles, between the windows of the cupola, are represented the Christian virtues ... Beneath them ... are placed the four Evangelists ... and, finally, beneath their feet ... the four rivers of Paradise ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose layers of symbolic detail (virtues, evangelists, paradise imagery) beneath principal scenes to deepen theological meaning and provide multi-level instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design must communicate core messages even to partial/viewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If he only entered, as often the common people do ... snatching a few moments before beginning the labor of the day to offer up an ejaculatory prayer, and advanced but from the main entrance as far as the altar screen, all the splendor ... smote upon it only that they might proclaim the two great messages--'Christ is risen,' and 'Christ shall come.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the most essential theological messages are legible and prominent enough to be received by hurried or partially-engaged worshippers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material richness appropriate to sacred symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: It was fitting that neither the gold nor the crystal should be spared in the adornment of it; that, as the symbol of the Bride, the building of the wall thereof should be of jasper, and the foundations of it garnished with all manner of precious stones ... the Book-Temple shone from afar off like the star of the Magi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use costly materials and lavish adornment where they function as theological symbols (the Church as Bride, scripture as treasure), making the building itself a visible testimony to sacred truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public placement of sacred testimony as moral witness to the city
rubrics_metrics.description: Men met there from all countries of the earth, for traffic or for pleasure; but, above the crowd ... was seen perpetually the glory of the temple, attesting to them ... that there was one treasure which the merchantmen might buy without a price ... The walls on which its testimony was written were separated but by a few inches of marble from those which guarded the secrets of her councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate religious art and inscriptions conspicuously in civic spaces so that they serve as continual moral and spiritual reminders to public life and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for losses and restorations when assessing authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: They all agree in another respect, as well as in style. All are either ruins, or fragments disguised by restoration. Not one of them is uninjured or unaltered; ... and the impossibility of finding so much as an angle or a single story in perfect condition is a proof ... that they were indeed raised during the earliest phases of the Venetian power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating historical architecture, distinguish original elements from modern restorations; restorations can obscure or destroy original proportional and stylistic evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Byzantine architectural features (forms and organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: They all agree in being round-arched and incrusted with marble ... continuous arcades along their entire fronts from one angle to the other, and in having their arcades divided, in each case, into a centre and wings; both by greater size in the midmost arches, and by the alternation of shafts in the centre, with pilasters, or with small shafts, at the flanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify Byzantine palaces by round arches, marble incrustation, continuous arcades, centre-and-wing composition, and alternation of shaft and pilaster as diagnostic formal criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtle gradations of proportion and cadence in arch dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an exquisite symmetry running through their apparent confusion; ... The way in which the large shaft is used as an echo of those in the central arcade, dovetailing them, as it were, into the system ... is highly characteristic of the Byzantine care in composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe minute, graduated differences in arch widths, shaft placements, and groupings (sometimes only inches) as intentional compositional devices; these subtle cadences are essential to Byzantine harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-functional minor elements to complete composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Byzantine builder could not be satisfied with so simple a group, and he introduced, therefore, two minor arches at the extremities, ... by adding two small porticos which are of no use whatever except to consummate the proportions of the façade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize architectural elements that exist primarily for proportional completion rather than function—their presence indicates an aesthetic priority for compositional balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty depends on subtle variations often beneath conscious detection
rubrics_metrics.description: The eye is continually influenced by what it cannot detect; nay, it is not going too far to say, that it is most influenced by what it detects least. ... The greater he is, the more he will feel their subtlety ... there is nothing truly noble either in color or in form, but its power depends on circumstances infinitely too intricate to be explained, and almost too subtle to be traced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for effects that may not be consciously noticed—small, intricate adjustments in line, proportion, and color can have outsized influence on perceived beauty; critics and restorers should attend to these subtleties.
